argv:
You generate synthetic meeting transcripts with gold annotations for LiveMinutes, a research dataset modeled on the AMI Meeting Corpus scenario meetings.

In AMI scenario meetings, a team of four plays a design team in a fictional company. The roles are Project Manager (PM), Marketing Expert (ME), User Interface designer (UI) and Industrial Designer (ID). A series has four meetings: (a) kickoff, (b) functional design, (c) conceptual design, (d) detailed design. Later meetings refer back to earlier ones.

Write natural spoken conversation the way AMI transcripts read: short turns, fillers ("um", "uh", "yeah"), backchannels ("mm-hmm", "okay"), interruptions, people building on each other, and some disfluency. Do not write a screenplay. Do not narrate. No stage directions.

Each segment is one dialogue-act-like unit: one speaker, usually one clause or short sentence, sometimes just a backchannel. Give each segment an AMI dialogue-act type from this set:
  bck backchannel, stl stall, fra fragment, inf inform, sug suggest, ass assess,
  el.inf elicit-inform, el.sug elicit-offer-or-suggestion, el.ass elicit-assessment,
  el.und elicit-comment-understanding, off offer, und comment-about-understanding,
  be.pos be-positive, be.neg be-negative, oth other

Absent participants NEVER speak. Speaker labels are ground truth: use only the labels you are given.

The gold annotations must be exactly true of the transcript you write. Refer to segments by their "n" number. Every number you cite must exist.

Output a single JSON object and nothing else: no prose, no markdown fences.

request.user:
Write meeting SY0203b: meeting "b" (functional design) of series SY0203.

PROJECT
The team is designing a children's educational tablet case.

PARTICIPANTS (label, role, status for this meeting)
A  Project Manager (PM)  Laura  present
B  User Interface designer (UI)  Tom  present
C  Marketing Expert (ME)  Priya  present
D  Industrial Designer (ID)  Marcus  ABSENT, never speaks

EARLIER MEETINGS IN THIS SERIES
Stay consistent with them. Refer back to them, follow up on their open action items, and keep the same product and team.

[SY0203a, kickoff]
  abstract: The project manager opened the kickoff meeting, introduced the team and presented the project: a protective case for a children's educational tablet that should be original, trendy and user-friendly. She gave the financial targets: a selling price of 30 euros and a maximum production cost of 15 euros per unit. The industrial designer noted that this is tight for a properly shockproof case. After an icebreaker drawing exercise, the team discussed first ideas: drop protection with rubber or foam and thick corners, a carrying handle, cutouts that keep the buttons and camera clear, a possible stand, and a wipeable material such as silicone or EVA foam. The team agreed to target children aged four to eight. The task of finding the tablet sizes the case must fit was first given to the industrial designer. It was then reassigned to the user interface designer, so the industrial designer could concentrate on materials.
  decisions: The target age group for the product is children aged four to eight.
  actions: The user interface designer will find the common tablet sizes and dimensions the case must fit. This task was reassigned from the industrial designer. The user interface designer will work out the basic functions the case needs to provide for the user. The marketing expert will research competitor cases and their prices. The industrial designer will research materials, such as foam versus silicone, and estimate what fits within the 15 euro production cost. The project manager will send round notes from the meeting. Checking safety regulations for children's products, such as small parts and choking hazards, was raised but nobody took it on.
  problems: It is unclear whether the case will fit one specific tablet or several models. The 15 euro production cost limit may make strong shock protection difficult. A stand was suggested but would add cost. It was not decided. A shoulder strap was suggested, with doubts about its suitability for four-year-olds. It was deferred to the next meeting. No one is responsible for checking child safety regulations.
  action item SY0203a.ai1: Find out which tablet sizes and dimensions the case needs to fit (owner B, reassigned)
  action item SY0203a.ai2: Research competitor tablet cases and their prices (owner C, active)
  action item SY0203a.ai3: Research case materials (foam vs. silicone) and estimate what fits within the 15 euro production cost (owner D, active)
  action item SY0203a.ai4: Work out the basic functions the case needs to provide for the user (owner B, active)
  action item SY0203a.ai5: Send round notes from the kickoff meeting (owner A, active)
  action item SY0203a.ai6: Check safety regulations for children's products (small parts, choking hazards) (owner no owner, active)
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The user interface designer proposed shaping the handle like animal ears. The marketing expert thought it might look too young, and it was not adopted.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The marketing expert suggested a carrying handle. The project manager liked it, but no formal decision was made.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The user interface designer suggested a stand for watching videos. The industrial designer noted it adds cost, and it was not decided.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The marketing expert suggested a wipeable material. The industrial designer mentioned silicone or EVA foam, and no material was decided.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The marketing expert suggested a shoulder strap. The project manager deferred it to the next meeting.
  fact (plan_change): The tablet sizes task was first assigned to the industrial designer and then reassigned to the user interface designer, because the industrial designer would be busy with materials.

EDGE CASES THIS MEETING MUST CONTAIN
Weave each one naturally into the project discussion. Each must be clearly present, and each must be tagged with the segments where it happens.
- F2_OFFERED_TAKEN_BY_OTHER [F2]: One person offers to do a task ("I could look into ..."), but a different person ends up taking it. The gold owner is the person who took it, and the history records the offer and the acceptance.
  Required gold labels: action_items, edge_cases.
- F2_TASK_TO_ABSENT [F2]: A task is assigned to a team member who is absent from this meeting. The gold action item owner is that absent participant.
  Required gold labels: action_items, edge_cases.

LENGTH
Between 90 and 140 segments.

GOLD LABELS
- summary: AMI-style abstractive summary in third person, using role names ("The project manager ..."). Sections: abstract (3-6 sentences), actions, decisions, problems (open issues). It reflects the meeting's FINAL state: corrected values, final plans, and no jokes or tangents reported as content.
- action_items: every task arising in the meeting. owner is the speaker label of the FINAL owner, and may be an absent participant. owner is null ONLY for a task nobody takes, with owner_unclear true. status is the final status: active, reassigned (owner changed; previous_owners lists earlier owners) or dropped. history lists the events in order. evidence_segments lists the supporting segments.
- qa_facts: atomic facts someone could later ask about ("Who was asked to ...?", "Did the team agree on ...?"). Include every decision (agreed true), every proposal nobody agreed to (type unagreed_proposal, agreed false), action items, removed action items, absences, and plan changes. Because this meeting follows earlier ones, include at least one fact of type reference_to_prior_meeting, with refers_to_meeting set, at a point where someone refers back to an earlier meeting. Do NOT write questions.
- edge_cases: one entry per edge case above, with its scenario_id and the segment numbers that contain it.

OUTPUT JSON SHAPE
{
  "segments": [{"n": 1, "speaker": "A", "da_type": "inf", "text": "..."}],
  "summary": {"abstract": ["..."], "actions": ["..."], "decisions": ["..."], "problems": ["..."]},
  "action_items": [{"n": 1, "description": "...", "owner": "C", "owner_unclear": false, "status": "active", "previous_owners": [], "history": [{"segment": 12, "event": "assigned", "by": "A", "owner": "C"}], "evidence_segments": [12, 13]}],
  "qa_facts": [{"type": "decision", "fact": "...", "agreed": true, "related_action_item": null, "refers_to_meeting": null, "evidence_segments": [40]}],
  "edge_cases": [{"scenario_id": "...", "segments": [20, 21, 22], "note": "one line on how it appears"}]
}
history events: proposed, offered, assigned, accepted, reassigned, dropped, restated. qa_facts types: decision, unagreed_proposal, action_item, action_item_removed, absence, plan_change, reference_to_prior_meeting, other. related_action_item is an action item's "n" or null. refers_to_meeting is an earlier meeting ID of this series or null.
